mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm really glad you're here with me. Imagine a world turned upside down by war, where innocence slips away, and every step forward is filled with questions about who you really are and what life means after everything changes. That’s the very heart of what we’re about to explore together, as we journey through Robert Graves’ powerful memoir, Goodbye to All That. Graves takes us right into the chaos of early twentieth-century Europe—into the trenches of World War I—where the old rules and comforts are swept away, and nothing feels certain anymore. But this isn’t just a war story. It’s also about trying to piece together a new sense of self when the world you once knew has vanished. We’ll walk alongside him through memories of childhood, the friendships and rivalries of school days, and the deep bonds formed between soldiers—set against the harsh reality of battle and the wounds that linger long after the fighting ends. As we move through the shifting landscape of postwar England, we’ll see how old values are tested, relationships are reshaped, and the search for belonging becomes more urgent than ever. Through moments of dark humor, raw honesty, and reflection, Graves invites us to look at how war changes not just nations, but the very core of a person. So, if you’ve ever wondered what it takes to rebuild after loss—or how memory and identity are shaped by the things we survive—you’re in exactly the right place. Let’s dive in together and see what we can discover.
